_comment: Accepted cross-platform attribute-effect findings, two kinds. DIVERGENCE ({fixture, platforms}): the control-diff verdict (active = the attribute changed the render, inert = it did not) disagrees across the platforms the attribute is declared for — semantic drift unless a deliberate platform idiom; the reason says which. UNIFORMLY-INERT ({fixture, verdict, declared}): a value the SSoT enumerates changes nothing on ANY platform — either it is the default rendering (say so in the reason) or it is dead/unimplemented everywhere. Unrecorded findings fail `jui conformance gate --cross-effect`; entries the measurement no longer supports are stale and must be pruned (`jui conformance cross-effect --update`). Reason 'unreviewed-initial-measurement' marks the initial-measurement backlog — consume it.

fixed in this train (web), fixture cannot see it: rjui rendered autoShrink as a VIEWPORT-relative clamp — `font-size: min(<size>px, max(<size*factor>px, 1vw))` — which is not a fit-to-box shrink at all. At the conformance viewport (1024px, 1vw = 10.24px) the 1vw term outran both floors, so fixture (0.25 -> 4px) and control (default 0.5 -> 8px) both computed 10.24px, 0 differing px. The same emit was a product defect: a 16px Label rendered at 8px on a 375px-wide viewport. Replaced by a measured fit (`@/generated/autoShrink`, hoisted ref + effect); browser-probed on the shipped build — a bounded box shrinks 16px -> 9.5px with no declared floor and to the declared floor with one, and a Label without autoShrink in the same box does not move. THIS fixture stays inert on web because its shape (width 200, height wrapContent) never overflows, so a correct implementation has nothing to do — `Label/autoShrink__true` loses its web control_diff entry for the same reason. Measurement fix: a bounded-height shape discriminates on web (owner: D). Family: autoshrink-needs-bounded-shape.
entries.note: Bound face measured with the static face: the bound emit moved the factor into the effect's dependency list, so it re-fits when the data changes — the old clamp multiplied it in Ruby and raised on a bound value.

entries.reason: android inert is the DEFECT, ios/web active is correct — CONFIRMED 2026-08-07 by E's formal reading, which found the declaration already says it and needed no SSoT change; the orchestrator's provisional ruling of the same day therefore stands and the hold on this row is lifted. The SSoT's Radio.checked precedence is `bound selectedValue > literal selectedValue > checked` and carries NO group term — `group` only selects which key the choice is stored under, and the declaration says `checked` seeds the group's INITIAL selection, selecting only while the group has made no choice yet. 51-C originally ruled the opposite (that a declared `group` suppresses the seed, so android was right) and was pushed back; 51-G read the declaration the same way E later confirmed and fixed android's dynamic path in KotlinJsonUI f3bdd90, with 51-C following on the codegen side (7c52cc8), so both android paths now compute `groupState || (seed && nothing chosen yet)`. Owners C (codegen) + G (dynamic), both landed, neither re-measured on device. The row drops when a 3PF run finds android active. Family: radio-group-seed-canon.
entries.note: Kept because the retraction is the lesson: 51-C's original ruling rested on 'two of the three implementations agree, so they are right', which is a majority vote over usage. Semantics come from the SSoT declaration alone — the same trap the design-principles ledger names — and here the declaration turned out to settle it outright, with E's confirmation changing nothing but the conditional this row used to carry.

G's measured mechanism is sharper than the original ruling: the items mode read `selectedValue` through the `TypedAttrs.undeclared(json, ...)` ESCAPE HATCH and looked only at the bound face — but the spelling IS declared on Radio (the item mode two lines over reads it through the typed accessor), so reaching for the undeclared hatch was itself the error. android render-stage gap on the DYNAMIC renderer, codegen innocent — merged from the two lanes that measured it from opposite ends (51-C codegen face, 51-G dynamic root cause). ios is OUTSTANDING against the canon, not correct-by-default — rewritten 2026-08-07 on the orchestrator's ruling after 51-F pushed back on the previous reason. The previous text said '`fill` is SwiftUI's stack default, so ios has nothing to change'; attribute_semantics.json#distribution does not say that. It maps fill.swiftui to `.frame(maxWidth/maxHeight: .infinity) on each child`, states that 'web landed first and is the reference implementation; ios (sjui view_converter.rb ...) and android ... are outstanding', and records from the re-measure that '`fill` stays inert on ios: with the child width gone the fixture can finally demonstrate it, and ios does not.' The default reading also mixes up two frameworks: filling is UIStackView's default, not SwiftUI's — a SwiftUI HStack does not grow its children. The `observable` block's {ios: inert} is the RECORD OF A MEASUREMENT, not an acceptance; the same ruling says the entry 'gets re-measured, not edited'. So this row stays, with the correct owner: F implemented the canon on the ios dynamic path (SwiftJsonUI 440c06a, childData channel so the frame lands inside each child's own modifier chain, explicitChildSizeWins honoured on the read side), and B owns the codegen half (sjui view_converter.rb still emits nothing for fill). The row drops when a 3PF run measures ios active — by measurement, not by edit. Family: distribution-size-half-outstanding.
